threads.name: Beautiful design & making
threads.want: Calm, well-shot videos of a person designing or making a physical object start to finish: product and industrial design, furniture, leatherwork, shoemaking, small-space architecture. Process shown on camera, design decisions explained, aesthetic payoff at the end.
threads.avoid: Quick craft hacks, '5-minute crafts' style, product unboxings or reviews, home tours with no making, DIY fails, rambling vlogs with little work on screen

threads.name: How things are designed
threads.want: Design thinking beyond making things by hand: industrial designers explaining their process and sketches, why everyday objects, buildings, cities, interfaces and type look the way they do, design history and critiques of good and bad design. Clear point of view, well shot, leaves me with a way of seeing I can use in my own design work.
threads.avoid: Software tutorials and 'learn Figma in 10 minutes', logo speed-art, portfolio-review drama, 'design tier lists', dropshipping product 'designs', AI image generator hype, home decor hauls
seedSearches: why this object is designed this way
the design of everyday things explained
architect explains why this building works

threads.name: How companies win
threads.want: Clear, researched breakdowns of how real companies and products win or fail: strategy, pricing, operations, supply chains, business models, founder decisions. Teaches a way of thinking I can reuse, backed by numbers and history.
threads.avoid: Hustle gurus, podcast clips, 'how I made $X in 30 days', passive income, crypto, stock tips, 'this stock will explode', drama about CEOs with no analysis, AI-voiceover business channels
seedSearches: how this company actually makes money

threads.name: Building with Claude
threads.want: Practical videos that make me better at building things with Claude, Claude Code and other AI coding tools: real projects built start to finish, workflows, prompting and agent techniques, talks from Anthropic and from experienced builders. Shows the actual screen and the actual result.
threads.avoid: AI hype and doom, 'AI will replace you', 'make $10k with ChatGPT', prompt-pack sellers, AI news roundups, model-vs-model benchmark clickbait, AI-voiceover channels, thumbnail-face 'this changes everything'
seedSearches: building an app with claude code
claude code tips from real projects

threads.name: Clever builds (tight edits)
threads.want: One person or small team engineering a weird or ambitious machine and showing the real problem-solving: CAD, failed prototypes, the fix, the test. Has to keep moving; a clear goal stated early and a payoff by the end.
threads.avoid: Videos over 25 minutes, slow multi-part builds, 'I bought X from AliExpress', sponsored gadget showcases, pure destruction or crash videos without engineering

threads.name: Science & math aha
threads.want: One surprising idea in physics, math or how-the-world-works, explained with a demo or clean visuals and a real 'oh, that's why' payoff. Hooky premise in the first minute.
threads.avoid: Lecture recordings, homework walkthroughs, slideshow narration, AI-voiceover explainers, conspiracy or pseudo-science, videos longer than 25 minutes
seedSearches: why does this happen physics explained

threads.name: Wild projects vlogs
threads.want: A real person filming themselves doing a long hands-on project or adventure in the wild: building a cabin, fixing up machines, camping in odd places, surviving on a budget. Personality-driven, mostly self-shot.
threads.avoid: Pure ski or climbing films, gear reviews, survival 'challenges' with fake drama, compilation channels, 'Top 10 survival tips'
seedSearches: building a cabin alone in the woods

threads.name: Storytellers & behind the camera
threads.want: Well-crafted short-form stories from filmmaker-vloggers, plus behind-the-scenes breakdowns of how shots, edits and cinematography were actually done. Either a great story or you learn how a great story is made.
threads.avoid: Movie or TV clips, trailer reactions, 'ranking every movie', gear unboxings, prank vlogs, 24-hour challenge videos
seedSearches: how we shot this scene behind the scenes

threads.name: How small businesses actually work
threads.want: A specific real small business (shop, restaurant, trade, product brand) broken down with real numbers: costs, margins, what went wrong, how the owner fixed it.
threads.avoid: Hustle gurus, Hormozi or podcast clips, 'passive income', dropshipping, crypto, 'how I got rich at 22' with no numbers, Lambo or lifestyle flexing, Shark Tank clips
seedSearches: how much does a restaurant make
I tried to save a failing business

threads.name: Sports stories
threads.want: Documentary-style stories about athletes, rivalries and teams (F1, NBA, NFL, table tennis), plus the occasional table tennis technique or pro-player video. Narrative and context, not highlights.
threads.avoid: Raw highlight reels, hot-take debate shows, 'Ranking your takes' style, fight knockout compilations, gym-drama roast channels
seedSearches: how this team built a dynasty

threads.name: Watch dealing
threads.want: Entertaining watch dealing and flipping: negotiating, authenticating, real buy and sell numbers, plus occasional watch-brand history. Personality plus real money on the line.
threads.avoid: Affiliate 'best watches under $X' lists, unboxings, celebrity collection reaction clips, how-to-resize-bracelet tutorials

threads.name: Tech, MKBHD-style
threads.want: Polished, well-shot tech videos with a clear point of view about CURRENT products (released or relevant in the last ~12 months) or timeless topics: in-depth reviews, 'why this product matters', design and industry explainers about phones, laptops, cars, gadgets. Honest opinion, explains the tradeoffs, useful to someone deciding what to buy or understanding where tech is going.
threads.avoid: Reviews of old products (anything older than ~12 months unless the topic is timeless), unboxing-only videos, rumor and leak roundups, 'iPhone vs Android' fanboy fights, 'Top 10 gadgets under $50', AliExpress hauls, gift guides, AI-voiceover tech news, tutorials and settings tips

threads.name: Big creators, standouts only
threads.want: Main-channel uploads from a few big creators, only when the video is a genuine standout (strong performance vs their own average, a real project or challenge, not filler). Zero is fine on most days.
threads.avoid: Second-channel clips, shorts compilations, sponsored filler, merch drops, collab videos that are mostly another creator's content

globalAvoid: Shorts of any kind (under 3 minutes or vertical); livestreams and VODs; TV show and movie clips or compilations of any kind (Family Guy, The Office, Parks and Rec, SNL, The Boys, A&E reality like Squatters or Intervention, Bar Rescue, Shark Tank); reaction videos; 'X DESTROYS Y' political or religious debate bait; cringe compilations and roast channels; streamer clip channels and GTA or gaming content; AI-voiceover channels; top-10 lists; get-rich and hustle content; shocked-face clickbait titles with no substance.
notes: Main goal is to watch less YouTube overall and eventually replace it, not to find more to watch. Every pick should give me something (skill, idea, story, craft), not just kill time like the TV clips I used to watch. Bingeing happens on empty days. Budget follows Google Calendar: free 75 / normal 30 / busy 20 minutes, holding through Jan 3, 2027, then tapering to floors of 30 / 20 / 15. Quality over filling the quota: if nothing strong comes up, show fewer videos. Goes through phases, so a thread that gets several thumbs-downs in a row should pause itself for a couple of weeks. Prefers videos under ~25 min; long builds feel slow. Loves good-looking, well-filmed design and craft videos. Viewing: clicking a pick opens just that video on its own page (embedded player, no sidebar, no recommendations, no comments, no autoplay; rel=0 and cover the end screen). Never link out to youtube.com's watch page.
